answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it can earn reputation or vote, then slash that stake when independent audits prove coordinated fraud. Auditors sample claims across an island of activity and check signed records against a shared cipher-based commitment, so one operator cannot cheaply multiply identities and manufacture trust. A sybil attacker must fund every identity and risk losing the stake; spreading influence across a longer voyage raises that cost without pretending identity checks are perfect.
